sm: Judicial Watch says newly unsealed court records show a broad federal criminal investigation of Representative Ilhan Omar, covering conduct from 1980 to the present, tied to the October 12 search of her Washington residence. Chief Judge James Boasberg ordered the release on November 23 of 169 pages, more than half entirely blacked out, and the Justice Department still withholds much of the warrant, its attachments and the inventory of seized items. The group says the Justice Department told the court it believes Omar has committed crimes over decades, though the specific statutes are redacted. Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh pressed for more on probable cause, held the warrant for a week, raised the Speech or Debate Clause himself, ordered extra briefing, and signed on October 9. Senior Justice Department officials, including an Associate Deputy Attorney General, signed the filings.

The warrant authorized seizure of Omar's phones, computers and records, and the government warned that disclosure could lead other potential subjects to flee or destroy evidence, though the records do not name anyone else. Homeland Security Investigations executed the warrant on October 12, and the Justice Department later said the investigation was still in full swing and the warrant not fully executed. Judge Sharbaugh rejected the department's argument that the Speech or Debate Clause did not apply and required a special search protocol. The department had pointed to an earlier, broader warrant against a redacted target with no such protections, which Judicial Watch suggests was a current or former member of Congress. Judicial Watch president Tom Fitton called the court's delay and special protections unusual. The group says its Omar inquiry dates to a July 2019 ethics complaint, and it cites earlier unsealing efforts involving Mar-a-Lago, Mike Lindell and others.
